Each year's ERA5-Land snow over one watershed

Source: R/wet_snow_annual.R
wet_snow_annual.Rd

Reads cd's annual snow layers (one band per year, ERA5-Land at 0.1 degree) and returns each year's mean over a watershed: the per-year values that wet_snow_normals() averages over 1981-2010 onto a grid, here kept year by year and for one area.

Usage

wet_snow_annual(
  ws,
  vars = c("snowmelt_doy_50", "swe_max"),
  years = NULL,
  catalog = NULL,
  cap = c(swe_max = 3000)
)

Arguments

ws

terra::SpatVector of polygons, in any CRS: one watershed.

vars

cd variable names, each with an "annual" row in catalog, for example snowmelt_doy_50 (the day of the year by which half the year's snowmelt has happened), swe_max (the year's peak snow water equivalent, mm) or snowmelt_rate_peak (the peak weekly melt rate, mm per week).

years

Years to return; every one must be a band of each variable's file. NULL returns every band year of the first variable, which every other variable must also have.

catalog

A data.frame with columns variable, period and href, as from cd::cd_catalog(); NULL reads cd's default catalog. A remote href is read through cd::cd_cache_fetch(); any other must be a local file.

cap

Named numeric: an upper limit for each cell's value of each named variable, applied in every year before the mean. Variables not named are not capped. The default caps swe_max when it is in vars; a cap given explicitly must name only variables in vars.

Value

data.frame(year, <vars>, cover), one row per year in ascending order. cover is the same in every row; where it is 0 the values are NA.

Details

ws is one watershed, given as its fundamental watersheds (as fetched from fwapg) or as a single outline. The polygons are dissolved into one with terra::aggregate() and that union is sampled once with wet_ws_sample() (method = "area"), so the fundamental watersheds and their union as terra::aggregate() returns it give identical results, and nested or overlapping polygons count their ground once. A union stored and read back (as WKT, say) agrees to the rounding of its coordinates. Several watersheds passed together return the mean over their union; call once per watershed for separate values.

The mean weights each cell by the share of that 0.1-degree cell the watershed covers, as wet_ws_sample() does, not by the cell's ground area. A cell's area shrinks with latitude, by about 2.4 % per degree at 54 N, so for a watershed spanning half a degree of latitude the two weightings differ by about 1 % between its north and south edges; for one spanning many degrees, cells to the south are underweighted by more.

Each variable and year is one layer of a single stack, so wet_ws_sample()'s rule holds across all of them: a cell counts only where every layer has a value, and cover is one number, the share of the watershed on those cells. A cell missing in one year or one variable therefore leaves every year's value over the remaining cells, and a year's value can depend on which years and vars are asked for. ERA5-Land has no cell over the sea, so a watershed reaching the coast can report cover below 1.

cap limits each cell's value in each year before the mean, as wet_snow_normals() limits each cell's 1981-2010 mean: ERA5-Land's glacier points carry perennial snow, with swe_max of 5,000 to 10,000 mm against a seasonal maximum of about 3,000 mm elsewhere.

See also

wet_snow_normals() for the 1981-2010 means on a grid.

Examples

# Maxan Creek above Bulkley Lake (08EE018) and cd's layers cropped to it,
# bundled with wet (data-raw/snow_pilot_data.R)
d <- system.file("extdata", "snow_pilot", package = "wet")
outline <- readRDS(file.path(d, "maxan_outline.rds"))
ws <- terra::vect(outline$wkt, crs = outline$crs)
cat <- utils::read.csv(file.path(d, "catalog.csv"))
cat$href <- file.path(d, cat$href)
snow <- wet_snow_annual(ws, c("swe_max", "snowmelt_doy_50"), catalog = cat)
head(snow)
#>   year  swe_max snowmelt_doy_50 cover
#> 1 1950 222.3437        142.0184     1
#> 2 1951 223.9557        129.9008     1
#> 3 1952 231.5902        136.5852     1
#> 4 1953 195.6545        132.3004     1
#> 5 1954 310.2845        144.5180     1
#> 6 1955 204.3500        148.6459     1
# peak snow and melt date over 2011-2025 against 1950-1980
rbind(early = colMeans(snow[snow$year <= 1980, 2:3]),
      late = colMeans(snow[snow$year >= 2011, 2:3]))
#>        swe_max snowmelt_doy_50
#> early 258.7510        138.3252
#> late  248.8356        128.5111
